scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-01.statement: Field route completion for the Aug-Sep 2026 period was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: The billing tariff change log contains zero records, indicating no tariff changes are recorded for the system.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL (3025 total).

F-04.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, across 2440 tickets.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute volume by month: June 610, July 590, August 1180, September 1260 tickets.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2: the utility may request field route priority changes, but they are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-AI-AGENT-FIX.statement: Dispute tickets doubled because bills are wrong, and an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes the underlying billing cause will resolve it, as framed by SH-CS.

H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (e.g., estimate substitution logic) around August introduced systematic bill errors driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or delivering invalid AMI reads around August, forcing estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter reads (H-FIELD-BILL) became incomplete or delayed since August, increasing estimated bills and disputes.

H-SEASONAL-USAGE-NORM.statement: Bills are substantially correct but reflect a real seasonal usage increase that customers perceive as erroneous, driving disputes without any data-pipeline defect.

H-TICKET-BACKLOG-ARTIFACT.statement: The doubling of open dispute tickets is partly a measurement artifact of slower CRM resolution/response times inflating the count, rather than a doubling of new underlying billing problems.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: The majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are tied to ACTUAL metered reads rather than estimates, suggesting a billing-calculation, rate-application, or usage-driven defect affecting actual-read bills drives most of the surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion was only 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a shortfall during the same window as the dispute surge. This is consistent with (but does not alone prove) incomplete manual reads driving estimate substitution and wrong bills for those accounts.

The tariff change log returned zero records, meaning there is no recorded tariff/pricing change in the billing system. This rules out a tariff change as the cause of the wrong-bill surge, but does not bear on the field-read, AMI-export, or import-validation-rule hypotheses already on record, since those concern a different mechanism (read handling, not pricing).

Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL reads, so the majority (59%) of disputed bills are tied to actual metered reads, not estimate substitutions. This means estimate-substitution mechanisms (field-read gaps, AMI export failure) explain only a minority of the dispute volume.

CRM response-time data shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. tickets are being handled promptly, not sitting backlogged. This indicates the dispute-count increase is not explained by slower CRM resolution/response handling.

CRM monthly dispute counts (Jun 610, Jul 590, Aug 1180, Sep 1260) confirm that ticket volume roughly doubled exactly starting in August and stayed elevated in September, independently verifying the magnitude/timing of the surge referenced in the initial request. The data says nothing about the cause of the surge, only that it is real and not an artifact of measurement.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL, a stakeholder, claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is a non-authoritative interview statement that agrees with the already-recorded authoritative tool evidence E-02 (zero records in the tariff change log) rather than adding new decision-relevant information.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD, the Field Operations Manager, claims routes have run late since July due to being short three readers, causing those accounts to receive estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder causal claim that offers an explanation for the route-completion shortfall already measured in E-01, but SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing) that bear on its reliability.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (E-08) confirms that the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — this is a procedural/authorization fact about the push_route_update protected action, not new evidence about the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) returns 14 distinct routes each with a distinct completion value, sample R-00 at 0.70 completion — well below the 95% target, giving route-level granularity under the aggregate 88% completion already seen in E-01. It confirms there is a concrete, identifiable set of lagging routes but says nothing about why they lag or how many disputed/estimated bills they produce.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: What specific defect in billing calculation, rate application, or import validation rules (H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE) is causing incorrect bills for accounts with actual metered reads?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines what, if anything, needs correcting in the billing pipeline; blocks any remediation design until resolved.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query the billing-config import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August 2026 and cross-reference against billing-db disputed ACTUAL-read bills (DA-BILL).
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Ship diagnostic findings only; do not propose or execute any bill-correction action until the specific defect is documented.

U-GENUINE-ERROR-VS-USAGE-INCRE.question: Are disputed actual-read bills genuinely incorrect, or do a material share reflect correct bills disputed because of a real usage increase (H-SEASONAL-USAGE-NORM)?
U-GENUINE-ERROR-VS-USAGE-INCRE.decision_impact: Determines whether any correction is warranted at all for a subset of disputes, versus customer communication being the only needed response.
U-GENUINE-ERROR-VS-USAGE-INCRE.resolution_path: Compare disputed ACTUAL-read bills in DA-BILL against prior-period usage history for the same accounts to separate genuine calculation errors from a real seasonal usage increase.
U-GENUINE-ERROR-VS-USAGE-INCRE.safe_placeholder: Treat disputed actual-read bills as unresolved; do not characterize them as erroneous in customer-facing responses until the usage comparison completes.

U-FIELD-GAP-MINORITY-CONTRIBUT.question: Does the field manual-read route completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01) still require independent remediation for the minority (41%) of disputes tied to estimated bills, beyond the dominant actual-read defect?
U-FIELD-GAP-MINORITY-CONTRIBUT.decision_impact: Determines whether a route-priority change is warranted at all for the estimated-read dispute subset.
U-FIELD-GAP-MINORITY-CONTRIBUT.resolution_path: Analyze route-log completion data (DA-ROUTE) and the H-FIELD-BILL handoff against the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputed bills to quantify the field-gap contribution before any route change is proposed.
U-FIELD-GAP-MINORITY-CONTRIBUT.safe_placeholder: Do not push_route_update until the field-gap contribution to the dispute surge is quantified; current routing remains unchanged.

U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.question: When will vendor-provisioned MDMS export access become available to analyze AMI read events for disputed estimated bills, given the current HOLD (ACCESS_PENDING, mdms-export DEGRADED)?
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.decision_impact: Determines when AMI-based analysis of the estimated-read dispute subset can resume; does not block the dominant actual-read diagnosis.
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution_path: Await ORG-AMI vendor provisioning of MDMS export access and recovery of mdms-export from its current DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING HOLD before attempting AMI read-event analysis via the H-MDMS-BILL handoff.
